prov_le_tuyen.name: Lễ Tuyền
prov_le_tuyen.lore: Low grassland by the shore of Triêu Hà Hồ and the gulf, where Lễ Tuyền Phái keeps its spring. Its people farm rice, tend the school's herb beds and carry its wine jars to the boats. Envoys of the Pivot come each year for the wine, and a warm spring nearby is where they are made to wait.

prov_p148.name: Thủy Điền
prov_p148.lore: The oldest rice country of the plain, flooded paddies and dry steppe along a river under the western hills. Its farmers have planted here since 140 and still set the plain's first seedling each spring. A spirit vein runs under the dry ground beyond the paddies.

prov_p149.name: Âu Lộ
prov_p149.lore: A low marsh coast and oak woods on the eastern gulf, loud with nesting birds. Its people fish from the shore; their forebears were the pearl divers of Châu Lệ Cảng and never dived again. A water vein lies in the woods behind the marsh.

prov_p150.name: Ngân Hạnh
prov_p150.lore: Grass and oak woods on a river at the western edge of the plain, rising to the hills. Its people farm rice and roast ginkgo nuts for the road. In the woods toward the hills stand the walls of a music town that emptied when Cửu Thiều fell.

prov_p151.name: Lý Hoa
prov_p151.lore: A broad sandy coast of grass and steppe on the eastern gulf, with the burned pearl harbour of Châu Lệ Cảng on its shore. Its people fish and grow white plums. Since the pirate years a hall of watchers has kept the coast, and its lantern still burns over the old oyster beds.

prov_p152.name: Hoàng Ngưu
prov_p152.lore: Open grass and steppe on the gulf where yellow oxen graze in loose herds. Its herders breed the oxen that plough the plain and pull its barges. A warm spring in the steppe is where the oxen are washed before the spring blessing.

prov_p41.name: Lai Nghi
prov_p41.lore: Dry steppe and grass around Phượng Minh's port city at the river mouth, with the broken walls of Vân Môn Thành upriver. Its people farm, herd and work the gulf trade. A fire vein under the steppe is said to stir when the nine tiers play at dawn.

prov_p85.name: Hoàng Vân
prov_p85.lore: Rice land and oak forest on the river where the plain lies flattest, around Phượng Minh's granary city. Its farmers bring their harvest to the round granaries by barge. Spirit boars come out of the forest at harvest, and the granary keepers pay hunters to meet them.

prov_p86.name: Đạo Hương
prov_p86.lore: Rice fields and woods running from a river to the gulf, with steep hills behind. The Vương family has planted a new field here every generation since 520. A clear lake in the woods reflects the hills so exactly that the Vương paint it on their betrothal letters.

prov_p87.name: Lục Dã
prov_p87.lore: Green meadows and steppe on the gulf with hills to the west, given to Lễ Tuyền Phái for its herb gardens in 662. Its people grow and dry healing herbs. A millstone town in the hills above was buried by a landslide in 1062.

prov_r17_1.name: Hồng Thổ Hoang
prov_r17_1.lore: High mountains and red badlands at the north-western corner of the plain, dry and bare. No one lives here but copper miners in season. Its peak is named for the vermilion bird of the south.

prov_r17_10.name: Hoàng Lương
prov_r17_10.lore: Dry steppe and grass on the inland hills west of Lai Nghi, without a river. Its people grow millet and herd goats. Jackal packs den on a rise near the village.

prov_r17_11.name: Thủ Mạch Lĩnh
prov_r17_11.lore: High mountains running to the coast at the plain's western border with the heart, where Đan Sơn Mạch lies. No villages stand here; Phượng Minh's guards and cinnabar miners are its only people. The palace has kept the ridge guarded since Thính Vũ Lâu's attack in 1150.

prov_r17_12.name: Phong Mật
prov_r17_12.lore: Hill meadows and forest above the plain, cool and flowery. Its people keep bees and sell honey and wax to the towns. Golden eagles nest on the cliff above the village.

prov_r17_13.name: Tử Thái
prov_r17_13.lore: Flat steppe and grass on the southern gulf shore, barely above the sea. Its people gather laver from the rocks and fish the shallows. The burned walls of a salt town stand on the shore, destroyed by Thôn Hải in 764.

prov_r17_14.name: Hàm Trạch
prov_r17_14.lore: Low steppe and grass on the southern gulf, some of it below the tide. Its people make salt in shallow pans and herd a few cattle. Red ants the size of a hand build mounds on the grass behind the pans.

prov_r17_2.name: Thúy Bình Lĩnh
prov_r17_2.lore: High mountains with forest and bamboo on the western edge of the plain, rising like a screen behind Hoàng Vân. No one lives here; jade miners come up in summer. The plain's farmers read the weather by the cloud on its peak.

prov_r17_3.name: Tùng Ngạn Lĩnh
prov_r17_3.lore: Mountains and forest falling to a small stretch of western coast. No village stands here; marble is quarried at the shore. Its peak looks like an ox lying down, and the herders of Hoàng Ngưu bow to it.

prov_r17_4.name: Trùng Loan Lĩnh
prov_r17_4.lore: Fold after fold of high mountain and forest on the western coast, empty of villages. Woodcutters and herb gatherers work its lower slopes. Its tallest peak carries the sound of Lai Nghi's dawn bells back across the plain.

prov_r17_5.name: Nhật Xuất
prov_r17_5.lore: Grass and steppe at the far eastern end of the plain, facing the open sea. Its people fish and are the first on the plain to see the sun each morning. A fire vein in the grass is warmest at dawn.

prov_r17_6.name: Liệt Nhật Lĩnh
prov_r17_6.lore: High mountains on the western gulf coast, hot and bare on their sunward side. No one lives here. Phượng Minh's fire disciples sit on its peak at noon in summer.

prov_r17_7.name: Hải Mục
prov_r17_7.lore: Wide grass and steppe on the gulf coast east of Lai Nghi, some of it below the tide. Its people graze cattle on the salt grass and fish the shore. Wild iron-horned buffalo roam the grass inland.

prov_r17_8.name: Thâm Tỉnh
prov_r17_8.lore: Dry steppe and grass inland on the eastern plain, without river or coast. Its people live by deep wells and graze sheep and oxen. An earth vein runs under the steppe near the village.

prov_r17_9.name: Thú Hải Lĩnh
prov_r17_9.lore: Mountains and grass on the western gulf coast, overlooking the plain. No village stands here; the broken fort that watched for Thôn Hải's sails sits on its seaward side. Its peak looks down on the rice fields like a bowed head.

prov_le_tuyen_hot_spring_1.name: Cam Lộ Thang
prov_le_tuyen_hot_spring_1.look: A warm spring in the grass near the lake, edged with white stone and shaded by a small roofed pavilion.
prov_le_tuyen_hot_spring_1.lore: Lễ Tuyền Phái bathes its fever patients here before they drink the wine. The Pivot's envoys are given the pavilion while the jars are sealed.

prov_p148_spirit_vein_1.name: Hòa Miêu Mạch
prov_p148_spirit_vein_1.look: A patch of dry steppe beyond the paddies where grass grows green in the driest month.
prov_p148_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein under the dry ground. Thủy Điền's farmers raise their first seedlings here before planting them out.

prov_p149_spirit_vein_1.name: Thanh Âu Nhãn
prov_p149_spirit_vein_1.look: A small clear spring in the oak woods behind the marsh, where gulls come to drink and bathe.
prov_p149_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Thủy (water) vein rises here. The old divers' families say the pearls of Châu Lệ came from the same water.

prov_p150_spirit_vein_1.name: Kim Diệp Mạch
prov_p150_spirit_vein_1.look: A low grassy mound near the river, ringed by young ginkgo trees that turn gold before any others.
prov_p150_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein. The villagers say the great ginkgo of Ngân Hạnh draws its long life from it.

prov_p150_ruin_2.name: Ngọc Quản Trấn
prov_p150_ruin_2.look: Low walls in the oak woods at the foot of the hills, with a carved stone stage still standing in the old square.
prov_p150_ruin_2.lore: A town of Cửu Thiều Cung where jade pipes were cut and played. When the palace fell its people left within a year, like those of Vân Môn, and the woods took it.

prov_p151_spirit_vein_1.name: Bạch Nhạn Huyệt
prov_p151_spirit_vein_1.look: A shallow hollow in the steppe where the snow geese land each spring, the grass pale and stiff.
prov_p151_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Kim (metal) vein lies under the hollow. The fishers say the geese come for it, not for the plum blossom.

prov_p151_minor_seat_p.name: Vọng Triều Đường
prov_p151_minor_seat_p.look: A walled hall of grey stone on the steppe shore, with a tall lantern tower facing the sea and the burned piers of Châu Lệ.
prov_p151_minor_seat_p.lore: A minor sect founded in 790 by survivors of the pirate years, sworn to Phượng Minh, which keeps watch on the eastern gulf and lays sea-ward formations against storms and raiders. Its lantern burns every night over the old oyster beds, and its head swears no harbour on this coast will burn again.

prov_p152_hot_spring_1.name: Ngưu Dục Trì
prov_p152_hot_spring_1.look: A broad warm pool in the steppe, its banks trodden bare by hooves.
prov_p152_hot_spring_1.lore: Hoàng Ngưu's herders wash the ox with painted horns here before walking it round the corral on the first day of spring.

prov_p41_spirit_vein_1.name: Cửu Tấu Mạch
prov_p41_spirit_vein_1.look: A low ring of standing stones on the steppe outside the city, the grass inside it scorched brown.
prov_p41_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein. Lai Nghi's musicians say it warms when the welcome is played nine times at dawn; no one has proved otherwise.

prov_p85_beast_lair_1.name: Dã Trư Lâm
prov_p85_beast_lair_1.look: Oak forest with its floor torn up in long furrows and the trunks rubbed bare and muddy.
prov_p85_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit boars with tusks like sickles live here and raid the rice at harvest. Hoàng Vân's keepers pay a bounty for every pair of tusks.

prov_p86_lake_1.name: Minh Kính Hồ
prov_p86_lake_1.look: A still lake in the woods behind the rice fields, reflecting the hills so exactly that the shore line is hard to see.
prov_p86_lake_1.lore: The Vương of Đạo Hương paint it on their betrothal letters; the one sent to the Tạ in 1199 bore it too.

prov_p87_lake_1.name: Bạc Hà Đàm
prov_p87_lake_1.look: A spring-fed pool in the meadows, its shallow edges thick with wild mint.
prov_p87_lake_1.lore: Lễ Tuyền's herb growers draw water for the beds from it, and the meadows smell of its mint after rain.

prov_p87_ruin_2.name: Thạch Ma Trấn
prov_p87_ruin_2.look: Half-buried walls in a landslide scar on the hillside, with round millstones lying among the rubble.
prov_p87_ruin_2.lore: A quarry town that cut millstones for the rice mills of the plain. In the great rains of 1062 the hillside slid and buried it in a night; the survivors went down to Lục Dã.

prov_r17_1_peak_1.name: Chu Tước Phong
prov_r17_1_peak_1.look: A bare red peak above the badlands, its rock shading from orange to deep crimson.
prov_r17_1_peak_1.lore: Named for the vermilion bird of the south. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire).

prov_r17_1_mine_2.name: Chu Đồng Khoáng
prov_r17_1_mine_2.look: Open copper workings in red badland rock, the spoil streaked green.
prov_r17_1_mine_2.lore: Its copper goes to Lai Nghi for the bells of the nine tiers.

prov_r17_10_village_1.name: Hoàng Lương Thôn
prov_r17_10_village_1.look: A dry hill village of mud-walled houses among fields of tall yellow millet.
prov_r17_10_village_1.lore: Its people grow millet and herd goats. Travellers who nap at its inn while the millet cooks are teased that they will dream a whole life before supper.

prov_r17_10_beast_lair_2.name: Quần Sài Cương
prov_r17_10_beast_lair_2.look: A low grassy rise pocked with dens, where gaunt red-brown jackals watch the road.
prov_r17_10_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit jackals hunt in packs here and follow travellers at a distance. The goatherds bring their flocks in before dark.

prov_r17_11_mine_1.name: Đan Sa Quật
prov_r17_11_mine_1.look: A guarded grotto in red rock below the ridge, its walls glittering crimson in torchlight.
prov_r17_11_mine_1.lore: Phượng Minh digs cinnabar here near the vein, under guard since the war of 1150. Its cinnabar goes to the palace's alchemists.

prov_r17_12_village_1.name: Phong Mật Thôn
prov_r17_12_village_1.look: A hill village among flowering meadows, its walls lined with log beehives.
prov_r17_12_village_1.lore: Its beekeepers sell honey and wax to Lai Nghi and Hoàng Vân, and Lễ Tuyền buys its honey for wine.

prov_r17_12_beast_lair_2.name: Kim Điêu Nhai
prov_r17_12_beast_lair_2.look: A cliff above the meadows whitened with droppings, great stick nests on its ledges.
prov_r17_12_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit golden eagles nest here and take lambs and goats from the hills. Young cultivators climb for the chicks and seldom manage it.

prov_r17_13_village_1.name: Tử Thái Thôn
prov_r17_13_village_1.look: A low shore village where dark sheets of laver dry on bamboo frames along the beach.
prov_r17_13_village_1.lore: Its people gather laver from the rocks at low tide and sell it pressed and dried.

prov_r17_13_hot_spring_2.name: Hàm Ôn Tuyền
prov_r17_13_hot_spring_2.look: A warm spring on the flat steppe, its rim crusted white with salt.
prov_r17_13_hot_spring_2.lore: Its water is salt and warm, and the laver gatherers soak their cracked hands in it.

prov_r17_13_ruin_3.name: Hải Diêm Trấn
prov_r17_13_ruin_3.look: Burned walls on the shore among old salt pans, the pans cracked and grown over with samphire.
prov_r17_13_ruin_3.lore: A salt town of the southern gulf, burned by Thôn Hải's pirates in 764, two years after Châu Lệ Cảng. Its salt makers never came back, and their pans lie dry.

prov_r17_14_village_1.name: Hàm Trạch Thôn
prov_r17_14_village_1.look: A village behind an earth bank below the tide line, its salt pans shining white beyond the houses.
prov_r17_14_village_1.lore: Its people make salt in shallow pans and sell it up the coast; the bank is raised a little every winter.

prov_r17_14_beast_lair_2.name: Xích Nghĩ Nguyên
prov_r17_14_beast_lair_2.look: Grassland studded with red earth mounds taller than a man, the grass around them stripped bare.
prov_r17_14_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit red ants the size of a hand build here, and a column of them can strip an ox to bone. The salt makers burn the grass between their bank and the mounds each dry season.

prov_r17_2_peak_1.name: Bích Tiêu Phong
prov_r17_2_peak_1.look: A high grey peak behind the plain, its top usually wrapped in a single white cloud.
prov_r17_2_peak_1.lore: Farmers read the weather by its cloud. Its qi runs Kim (metal).

prov_r17_2_mine_2.name: Mặc Ngọc Khoáng
prov_r17_2_mine_2.look: A summer working high on the mountain where black jade is cut from grey rock.
prov_r17_2_mine_2.lore: Its ink-black jade is carved into seals and inkstones for Phượng Minh's scribes.

prov_r17_3_peak_1.name: Ngọa Ngưu Sơn
prov_r17_3_peak_1.look: A broad forested mountain shaped like an ox lying with its head on its forelegs.
prov_r17_3_peak_1.lore: The herders of Hoàng Ngưu bow to it when they drive their oxen west. Its qi runs Thổ (earth).

prov_r17_3_mine_2.name: Vân Thạch Khoáng
prov_r17_3_mine_2.look: A marble quarry at the shore, its white blocks veined with grey like clouds.
prov_r17_3_mine_2.lore: Its cloud stone paves the courts of Hoàng Vân's counting hall and goes by boat along the gulf.

prov_r17_4_peak_1.name: Thần Chung Phong
prov_r17_4_peak_1.look: A tall peak above folded forest, its bare top shaped like an upturned bell.
prov_r17_4_peak_1.lore: On still mornings the bells of Lai Nghi's nine tiers echo back from it across the plain. Its qi runs Kim (metal).

prov_r17_5_village_1.name: Nhật Xuất Thôn
prov_r17_5_village_1.look: A fishing village on the far eastern shore, every door facing the sea.
prov_r17_5_village_1.lore: Its fishers launch at first light and say they see the sun before anyone else on the plain.

prov_r17_5_spirit_vein_2.name: Đông Thăng Nhãn
prov_r17_5_spirit_vein_2.look: A round patch of bare earth in the grass, warm at dawn and cold by noon.
prov_r17_5_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein that is strongest at sunrise. Phượng Minh's fire disciples come to sit in it before dawn.

prov_r17_6_peak_1.name: Kim Ô Phong
prov_r17_6_peak_1.look: A bare peak above the gulf whose sunward face shines gold at noon.
prov_r17_6_peak_1.lore: Named for the golden crow that lives in the sun. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire).

prov_r17_7_village_1.name: Hải Mục Thôn
prov_r17_7_village_1.look: A shore village behind a low dyke, its cattle grazing the salt grass right down to the tide.
prov_r17_7_village_1.lore: Its herders say salt grass makes the sweetest beef, and they fish when the cattle are in.

prov_r17_7_beast_lair_2.name: Thiết Giác Nguyên
prov_r17_7_beast_lair_2.look: Wide grass where a herd of huge dark buffalo grazes, their horns grey as iron.
prov_r17_7_beast_lair_2.lore: Wild spirit buffalo whose horns can split a cart. Hải Mục's herders keep their cattle well away from the herd's bulls.

prov_r17_8_village_1.name: Thâm Tỉnh Thôn
prov_r17_8_village_1.look: A steppe village gathered round a single deep stone well with a long sweep pole.
prov_r17_8_village_1.lore: Its people live by the well and their sheep. The well is so deep that a dropped stone is counted to ten before it splashes.

prov_r17_8_spirit_vein_2.name: Hậu Thổ Huyệt
prov_r17_8_spirit_vein_2.look: A low earth mound in the steppe topped by a small altar of piled stones.
prov_r17_8_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Thổ (earth) vein. The shepherds of Thâm Tỉnh pour the first water of every new well on its altar.

prov_r17_9_peak_1.name: Phủ Điền Lĩnh
prov_r17_9_peak_1.look: A high ridge whose crest bends forward over the plain like a bowed head.
prov_r17_9_peak_1.lore: Farmers say it bows to the first rice. Its qi runs Thổ (earth).

prov_r17_9_ruin_2.name: Liệu Phàm Bảo
prov_r17_9_ruin_2.look: A broken stone fort on the seaward slope, its signal tower toppled and its seaward wall gone into the gulf.
prov_r17_9_ruin_2.lore: Phượng Minh raised it in the pirate years to watch for Thôn Hải's sails. After the Purge the garrison was withdrawn in 790, and the empty fort crumbled.
